- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in subsequent forecasts; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 periods ahead.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for mean reversion in 3–5 period window and reduce forecast slope accordingly.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates true price in early periods (e.g., 1–5 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish — apply a “lead correction” by +1–2% for first 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33–1.00), model exhibits high variance; use median of recent 5-day forecast as anchor for correction, especially if true outcome deviates >2% from mean.
